answer: In a lagoon restoration market, each agent identity must lock a bond before it can claim paid work, and the protocol releases that bond only after a randomly assigned field task is verified by independent workers; confirmed duplicate identities forfeit their stake. An attacker minting N Sybils must tie up N bonds and risks losing each one, so capital at risk grows linearly with clones. A delta survey can be staged from one terrace, but every account still faces the same cost.
